name: shared_refusal_parity
description: THIS FIXTURE ASSERTS A REFUSAL, NOT AN OPERATION. Every case here is a cell in which BOTH engines left the mesh untouched, and the generator verified that by comparing the before and after dumps on coordinates, not on counts. Read it as 'this input is declined and the mesh survives intact' -- it is deliberately NOT counted as parity of a command's behaviour, and it will not redden if the command is deleted. Its mutation is the opposite one: remove the GUARD, and every case here goes red. Task 1220 adds `spin_two_edges_shared_face`, whose guard is the multi-edge spin TRANSACTION: delete the overlap check in commands/mesh/spin_edge.d and that case goes red on its face rings while its counts stay put -- a count-only check could not see it.

provenance.notes: Kept separate from the parity fixtures on purpose. 'Both engines did nothing' is its own measurement class; merging it into a parity suite is how a suite comes to contain cases that pass vacuously. CHANNELS: the sweep's comparison was never vertex-only -- it compared the vertex multiset, the edge multiset, faces BOTH as ordered rings (winding shows) and as unordered position sets, the material partition, the per-face 'did this face's own tag change', and the post-command selection. Re-checked independently over all 215 frozen cases: ZERO agree on vertices while differing on ordered face rings, so nothing frozen here is a vertex-channel-only agreement. PRECISION: the sweep compared at 1e-4 and this fixture's tolerance matches it. The actual reproduction is far tighter -- 208 of the 215 cases are bit-identical at the dumps' 6 decimals and the remaining 7 agree to 3e-6 or better, that being the worst deviation anywhere in the set. The tolerance is the MEASUREMENT's bound, not the data's.

cases.name: spin_two_edges_shared_face
cases.description: two interior edges whose face pairs OVERLAP -- (1,0,0)-(1,0,1) borders faces {0,1} and (2,0,0)-(2,0,1) borders {1,2}, so face 1 is named twice. A spin rewrites BOTH of its faces, so applying these one after the other makes the second act on a face the first replaced and the result depends on selection order. The reference cancels the whole command and leaves the mesh untouched (task 1121 sweep, cell `spin_two_edges`; ledger row 10). Its own control is `spin_two_disjoint` in spin_quads_geometry_parity.json -- the same two-edge gesture with DISJOINT pairs, where both engines spin both edges -- so what is declined here is the overlap and not multi-edge spin. Each of these two edges spins on its own. GEOMETRY CHANNEL ONLY: the reference's post-refusal selection was not captured, so none is frozen.
